cannibalisation_check.verdict: Partial, manageable overlap. No page targets 'validity', 'how long is a NOIM valid' or 'does a marriage certificate expire', and the SERP has no good answer. Write the spoke, strictly limited to time limits and expiry, and link up to the pillar. Not a case for merging, but if the pillar is later expanded with a validity table, this spoke should be redirected into it.

cross_market_insights: The head term 'marriage licence validity' has no relevant organic result in Sydney, Melbourne or Brisbane: Google shows a state law page, an XML dataset, a tax forum and a parliamentary PDF, with an image pack of Philippine marriage licence pages. The query is unserved.

The question variant 'how long is a noim valid' is served by celebrant pages and a Facebook post, most stating the NOIM is 'valid for 18 months', with three inconsistent versions (from lodgement, from the wedding date, before the wedding). Only the celebrant association frames it as a window. A clear, officially sourced correction is the gap.

PAA across all three cities leans toward proof and registration ('What happens to a marriage that is not registered?', 'What is the best proof of marriage?', 'Can I check my marriage status online?'): people asking about validity also worry whether their marriage counts. That ties to the persona fear of a wedding that is not a legal marriage.

Nobody connects the Australian time limits with the ones that bite destination couples: certificate copies that must be recent, CNIs and apostilles with a shelf life, and overseas licences that lapse (Greece and Italy six months per run-log, others to verify). A single 'what expires and when' table is our unique asset.
Volume is negligible (10 or fewer per variant), so the spoke should be tight, snippet-led and built for AI Overview and PAA capture, feeding authority to the pillar.
payload.recommended_angle: Most of your wedding paperwork does not 'expire', but almost all of it has a clock. Correct the '18-month validity' myth in the first 60 words, then give couples one clear map of every time limit that matters, at home and abroad: the NOIM window, what happens when the date moves, why the marriage certificate never expires but some offices want a recent copy, the shelf life of CNIs and apostilled documents, and how long licences last in the destinations Australian couples choose. Every figure sourced; the how-to stays in the pillar.
